ca_southeast_face_5.blurb: A broad granite slab on Mill Creek Dome, beside the Sonora Pass highway above Strawberry at roughly 6,900 feet. The face steps up in two tiers, with most of the lines on the steeper upper one and a few gentler ones below. Expect a friendly spread: about 29 climbs, mostly trad with a good share of bolted sport lines and a handful of top-ropes, running from very easy up to 5.9 and clustering in the 5.5 to 5.7 range. It is a good pick for newer leaders, early-season cragging and relaxed days on clean slab, and the walk in is short, roughly three quarters of a mile.

ca_south_star_wall.blurb: A steep granite cliff on Donner Summit above Truckee and Donner Lake, and the area's home for hard bolted climbing. Of the 29 routes here, 25 are sport and four are trad. There is almost nothing for beginners: a couple of 5.10s and a handful of 5.11s, then the bulk of the wall sits between 5.12 and 5.13, with a few climbs at 5.14. It suits strong sport climbers looking for sustained, powerful pitches on Sierra granite. Summer is the main season for the Summit, with spring and fall also workable, and the crags near the road keep walk-ins short.

ca_swan_slab_proper.blurb: A cluster of small granite boulders in Yosemite Valley, beside the Swan Slab crag across from the lodge and a short stroll from Camp 4. Nearly all of the 29 problems are bouldering, with one top-rope. The mix leans easy: lots of problems from VB to V2, a band at V3 and V4, and just a few harder ones up to V8. Lines include cracks, faces, a chimney, a lieback corner and a slab traverse, and the Sloth Boulder hand traverse is a well-known warm-up. Because it sits so close to the road and trail, expect company and spectators on busy days.

ca_hanging_garden_area.blurb: A small pocket of granite boulders on Mount Woodson, the ridge between Poway and Escondido in San Diego County. The area holds 29 climbs, 26 of them boulder problems plus three short trad lines. The grades stretch a long way, from easy V0 problems through a solid middle of V3 to V5 and on to a few hard testpieces up to V9. Woodson as a whole is known for hundreds of boulders on short, quality granite, and moving between them can mean a bit of scrambling and bushwhacking. Some landings are uneven or two-tiered, so bring pads and a spotter.

ca_mr_magoo_boulder.blurb: The best-known boulder in the Magoos group at Castle Rock State Park in the Santa Cruz Mountains, with 29 problems on Vaqueros sandstone. Most are moderate: a big block of VB to V2, a few V3 and V5, and a short tail of much harder lines. Holds are slopers, jugs and buckets, and the sandstone has the sculpted pockets and tafoni this park is known for. Expect fun, well-worn problems around the face that gives the boulder its name. It is a short walk up from the main parking lot, mostly shaded, and busy on weekends, quiet on weekdays.

ca_grotto_the_3.blurb: A deep, enclosed hollow in the cliffs of Table Mountain near Jamestown in the Sierra foothills, where three walls of columnar basalt meet. Of the 29 routes, 18 are trad and 10 are sport, with a single boulder problem. The grades start around 5.8 and are concentrated between 5.10 and 5.12, with one 5.13. The lower wall is largely crack and column climbing, while the overhanging upper wall carries mostly hard bolted lines reached by climbing up through the lower routes. The descent trail has loose blocks, so go in with care and be mindful of parties below.

ca_loading_zone_the.blurb: A roughly 70-foot crag of fine-grained basalt in Warner Valley, in the forest south of Chester near Lassen Volcanic National Park at about 5,200 feet. Most of the 28 climbs are trad, with five sport routes and two top-ropes, ranging from 5.7 to 5.12. The bulk fall between 5.8 and 5.10, which makes it a good place to practise placing gear. Tall trees give plenty of shade through the day. All routes finish on a large plateau with a walk-off. Not every top has bolted anchors, so carry extra slings if you plan to top-rope, and watch for loose rock and dirt.

ca_incredible_hulk.blurb: One of the largest granite walls in the High Sierra, on the Sawtooth Ridge above Little Slide Canyon near Twin Lakes and Bridgeport, at about 11,300 feet. Its faces rise roughly 1,200 feet, and most of the 28 climbs are long alpine-style trad routes of 5 to 13 pitches, with a pair of aid lines. Grades run from scrambling up to 5.13, with the weight of them between 5.10 and 5.13. This is a committed day or overnight objective: the walk in is long, the descent is a scramble with a rappel and loose scree, and the climbing is often compared to Yosemite Valley.
